| Scene description | • S12-A is in residential lanes in Yanzhi Road Community, Wuchang District. Five images were taken.<br>• S12-A-01, S12-A-03 and S12-A-04 show accumulations of white woven sacks, plastic bags, foam meal containers and cardboard against walls or electrical cabinets. Some bags read ‘High-gluten flour’ and ‘Maoya rice’.<br>• S12-A-02 shows four non-overflowing black bins labelled ‘Tianxingxiang Sanitation’ and ‘Residual waste’, with white foam-container-like waste nearby.<br>• S12-A-05 shows five black and green bins in a municipal waste classification shelter: two overflow and three do not. The older lanes have graffiti and notices, concrete paving and some weeds. |
| Regulatory basis | • Disposal points should be clean, without retained waste, wastewater or secondary pollution. Containers should be tidy, clearly labelled, checked and emptied before overflow, cleaned and disinfected regularly, and repaired or replaced when damaged. Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings, Section 4.5.4 Maintenance requirements (clause ID [D-16-C009](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Municipal waste should be classified at designated locations. Indiscriminate dumping, stockpiling, abandonment, scattering, spillage or burning is prohibited, as is mixing industrial, construction or medical waste or animal carcasses with municipal waste. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 12 (clause ID [D-08-C006](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Classification in disposal, collection and transport should be progressively implemented. Waste should be deposited at designated places and times; indiscriminate dumping, scattering and stockpiling are prohibited. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 15, Article 16 (clause ID [D-03-C001](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv), [D-03-C002](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Classification signs comprise four main categories—recyclables, hazardous waste, food waste and residual waste—and 11 subcategories, applicable to disposal, collection, transport and treatment. GB/T 19095–2019, Signs for classification of municipal solid waste1 Scope, 3 Sign category composition (clause ID [D-04-C001](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv), [D-04-C002](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Wuhan classifies municipal waste as recyclables, hazardous waste, food waste (wet waste) and residual waste (dry waste). Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 9 (clause ID [D-08-C003](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Indiscriminate dumping, scattering or stockpiling must cease and be corrected, with CNY 5,000–50,000 fines for organisations and up to CNY 200 for individuals. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 42 (clause ID [D-03-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Littering fruit remains, paper, cigarettes, cans, meal containers, gum or bags is prohibited. Hubei Provincial Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 19, items (2) (clause ID [D-05-C001](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)), Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 27, items (1) (clause ID [D-06-C006](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)). |
| Severity | **Severe.** Four accumulations and two overflowing bins are concentrated and conspicuous in older residential lanes with poor baseline sanitation. Bags and foam containers in concealed corners and beside electrical cabinets can cause pollution and encourage insects, constituting clear pollution and management failure. |
| Impact assessment | Visible effects: accumulations impair appearance; torn bags may release odours and attract insects and rodents. Overflow pollutes the ground and affects passage and living conditions. Near-term risks: delayed clearance may prompt complaints and increase vector breeding, especially as organic waste decomposes in cloudy, mild weather. |
| Potential causes | • Capacity or collection may be insufficient: two S12-A-05 bins overflow, while four S12-A-02 bins do not but have nearby accumulated waste, suggesting delayed collection or inappropriate allocation.<br>• Classification awareness or point locations may be inadequate: flour and rice packaging may have been discarded rather than placed in the proper bins.<br>• Management checks and maintenance may be inadequate: wall-side and electrical-cabinet accumulations remain uncleared, with weeds suggesting insufficient routine care.<br>• Check collection records, bin standards and complaints, and observe disposal behaviour and shelter use. |
| Long-term effects | Persistent or recurrent problems could worsen residential sanitation and health risks, reduce trust and participation in classification, expose managers to penalties under Article 42 of the Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, and result in designation as a priority remediation area with higher costs and adverse public perceptions. |
| Recommendations | • Immediate action: clear all accumulations and overflowing bins in S12-A-01 through S12-A-05, wash and disinfect the ground, repair or replace damaged bins, and add temporary disposal reminders beside the shelter.<br>• Longer-term action: (1) adjust bin capacity and numbers to actual waste generation, especially in dense lanes; (2) increase collection at peaks such as weekends and holidays; (3) promote classification through community notices and household visits; (4) establish daily recorded checks by property or sanitation operators and respond promptly; (5) explore scheduled disposal at designated locations. |
| Priority | **High.** Obvious accumulation and overflow cause visual and sanitation risks in residential lanes, affecting daily life and health. Respond immediately to prevent spread and escalating complaints; prioritise action to avoid liability under Article 42 of the Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste. |
